messages:
Maya: Quick note - we need a predictable way to 'surrender' a write when the resident region is unreachable, but without surprising product teams. Brainstorming.
Ethan: What about a three-mode write policy: `synchronous-resident`, `surrenderable`, `best-effort`. Synchronous blocks, surrenderable places an escrow+lease and returns a structured pending response, best-effort forwards and marks as non-resident.
Noah: Implementation sketch for surrenderable: local accept -> escrow row with seq + proof placeholder -> background 'handoff' tries resident persist -> on success mint resident-proof token and mark finalized -> on prolonged failure mark escrow as surrendered and emit audit event.
Sonia: UX: client should get explicit state: {status: pending|surrendered|finalized, seq, resident_hint}. SDK surfaces surrender reason and retry helpers.
compliance-bot: (automated) For tenants with residency clauses, `surrendered` reads must not expose PII. Product must map tenant flags to allowed write modes.
Ethan: Edge behavior: if tenant strict and resident unreachable -> immediately 503 with error code RESIDENCY_UNAVAILABLE. If tenant surrenderable -> return 202 with SURRENDERABLE policy and include ETA and escrow id.
Maya: Sequence constraints: prefer server-side monotonic per-tenant counter under a short lease. On takeover, new primary sets counter = max(stored, observed_highest + 1). Keep idempotency via client-supplied key too.
Noah: Ops concerns: we need a visible backlog metric `escrow.surrender.queue` and a runaway detector (alert if item age > threshold). Add admin controls: force-finalize, mark-surrendered, requeue.
Sonia: Audit/logging: every transition must emit an audit record with actor (system/ops/client), timestamp, and residency result. Retention per compliance = 730 days for EU tenants.
ops-bot: Heads-up: we'll add chaos test for region partition; will validate that surrenderable flows surface correct 202 vs 503 behavior.
Maya: I can write a short RFC follow-up capturing headers, response shapes, escrow schema, and runbook. Anyone want to pick implementation?
Ethan: I'll take the escrow table + handoff worker prototype.
Noah: I'll own the admin endpoints + telemetry dashboards.
Sonia: I'll update SDK surface and product docs.
compliance-bot: Acknowledged: will review RFC for contract language changes.
ops-bot: :thumbsup:
